stories.headline: Uttar Pradesh to set up mental health support cells in all universities and colleges
stories.deck: With the objective of providing students with a healthy, safe, and stress-free academic environment, a uniform Student Mental Health and Well-Being Policy will be prepared for all higher education institutions in the State
stories.bodyText:
Uttar Pradesh government on Monday (September 7, 2026) announced that a mental health support cell will be established in every university and college and a uniform policy for students’ mental health will be developed across higher education institutions.
“The Yogi Government has taken an important initiative regarding the mental health and well-being of students pursuing higher education in the State. With the objective of providing students with a healthy, safe, and stress-free academic environment, a uniform Student Mental Health and Well-Being Policy will be prepared for all higher education institutions in the State,” reads an official statement.
To discuss its effective implementation, Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay held a high-level meeting at his residence in Lucknow on Monday (September 7), in which various aspects of the proposed policy, expansion of mental health-related facilities in institutions, and an action plan for providing timely counselling and support to students were discussed in detail.
The government statement added that emphasis is on the overall personality development of students rather than limiting higher education to degrees and employment alone. “The objective of the proposed policy is to create an academic environment where students facing academic pressure, examination anxiety, career-related stress, or emotional difficulties can receive appropriate support in a timely manner.
Under the policy, a coordinated mental health support system will be developed at the state, district, and institutional levels. This will help provide students with access to counselling and specialist services according to their needs,” added the statement.
The official statement further reads, “Under the proposed framework, the Director of Higher Education will be designated as the nodal and implementing authority at the state level. A steering committee chaired by the Principal Secretary, Higher Education, will oversee policy implementation, budget allocation, and regular review. At the district level, a committee will be constituted under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate. This committee will coordinate with universities and colleges in the district and ensure effective monitoring and implementation of activities related to mental health and well-being. The most significant aspect of the Yogi Government’s proposed policy is the establishment of a Mental Health Support Cell in every higher education institution,”.

stories.headline: Night entry, lifting clothes don't amount to rape bid: Jharkhand HC
stories.deck: The Jharkhand High Court's decision emphasized that entering a woman's home after dark does not equate to attempted rape. The distinction made between criminally outrageous conduct and attempted rape is significant, resulting in upholding a conviction for offending modesty. The judge decided to lessen the sentence to time already served, thereby clarifying the legal nuances surrounding sexual…
stories.bodyText:
RANCHI: Entering a woman's house at night and trying to lift her clothes may be criminal, but it does not amount to an attempt to rape, Jharkhand HC has ruled while drawing a line between outraging a woman's modesty and attempting to rape her.
Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, deciding a criminal appeal on Aug 31, held that acts attributed to the appellant did not cross that legal threshold. HC upheld his conviction for using criminal force against a woman with the intention of outraging her modesty, finding evidence sufficient for the lesser offence. The judgement was released Monday.
The court modified a July 25 sessions court order from East Singhbhum district that had sentenced the man to four years of rigorous imprisonment for attempted rape. It reduced his sentence to the nearly eight months he had already spent in custody, saying that was sufficient to meet the ends of justice. The appeal was partly allowed.
The case dates to the night of Dec 26, 1999. The man was arrested on Dec 27 and later a chargesheet was filed alleging attempted rape.
The trial court convicted him of attempted rape and handed him a four-year prison term. The appellant approached the high court.
Justice Srivastava said an act can amount to attempted rape only when it is sufficiently proximate to the commission of rape. The evidence in this case did not make the leap from criminal force intended to outrage a woman's modesty to an attempt to rape, HC ruled.

stories.headline: Alternate fuels overtake petrol in passenger car sales
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India’s passenger vehicle market appears to be moving beyond the phase where alternative powertrains were a niche choice. In Aug, CNG, hybrid and 
electric vehicles
 together overtook petrol-powered cars for the first time, pointing to a broader change in how buyers are weighing fuel costs, technology and long-term ownership.
Alternative fuels accounted for 41.9% of passenger vehicle retail sales, edging past petrol at 40.8%, according to FADA. CNG was the biggest contributor with a 25.2% share, followed by hybrids at 9% and EVs at 7.6%. A year ago, petrol had led the alternative-fuel basket by nearly 11 percentage points. Diesel cars, meanwhile, accounted for 17.2% share of retail sales.
CNG biggest alternative to petrol
The crossover is significant because it is not being driven by a single technology. CNG has become the biggest alternative to petrol on the back of lower running costs, hybrids are finding more takers among buyers seeking better efficiency without depending on charging infrastructure, while EVs continue to expand their footprint.
FADA said running-cost economics and continuing hesitation around the E20 transition were nudging buyers towards CNG, hybrids and EVs. Petrol, however, remains the single-largest individual fuel type.
Among manufacturers, Maruti Suzuki dominated the CNG segment with around 71% share, while Tata Motors led electric passenger vehicles with around 43% share.
The shift is also visible beyond cars. In two-wheelers, EV penetration rose to 10.7% in Aug from 7.7% a year ago, crossing the 10% mark in a non-festive month for the first time. That suggests electric scooters are increasingly moving beyond early adoption and becoming part of the mainstream commuter market.
Three-wheelers are already much further along that transition. EVs accounted for 65.3% of sales in Aug, up from 56.6% a year earlier, making the category structurally electric. Commercial vehicles are starting from a much smaller base, but EV share more than doubled to an all-time high of 5.2% from 2.1%, indicating that electrification is beginning to move beyond pilots into fleet purchases.
Across all vehicle categories, EV retail sales reached 2.98 lakh units in Aug, up 52.9% year-on-year. The broader signal is that India’s mobility transition is no longer centred only on EVs; consumers are increasingly choosing from a wider mix of alternatives to petrol depending on use case, price and infrastructure.

stories.headline: Congress SC, ST MPs to petition President over Haldwani ‘purification’ row
stories.deck: MP Mallu Ravi said 32 MPs decided in a meeting to finalise a memorandum seeking the President’s intervention; they also decided to constitute a parliamentary forum to take up issues concerning SC and ST communities
stories.bodyText:
Thirty-two Congress MPs belonging to the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities on Monday (September 7, 2026) decided to petition President Droupadi Murmu over the alleged “purification yajna” held in Uttarakhand’s Haldwani following a rally addressed by party president Mallikarjun Kharge.
In a meeting at Indira Bhavan, the Congress headquarters, the MPs described the incident as a grave assault on the dignity and self-respect of SCs and STs and a direct affront to the constitutional values of equality and abolition of untouchability.
“We discussed the shocking purification incident in Haldwani following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally. We have decided to form a parliamentary forum to fight this at all levels. We will be submitting a representation to the President of India on Tuesday,” Lok Sabha member Mallu Ravi said.
The MPs finalised a memorandum seeking the President’s intervention and appropriate action. They also decided to constitute a parliamentary forum to take up issues concerning SC and ST communities.
Congress leaders K. Raju and Rajendra Pal Gautam also attended the meeting. Mr. Raju said the proposed forum would discuss a strategy for raising issues concerning SC and ST communities in Parliament.
The alleged ritual was held on August 11, three days after Mr. Kharge addressed a public meeting at the venue. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had condemned the incident and demanded an FIR be registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against those responsible.

briefs.headline: Delhi court sends Swatantra Bhardwaj to 14-day judicial custody
briefs.deck: Mr. Bhardwaj was produced before a Delhi court following the completion of his one-day police custody
briefs.bodyText:
A Delhi court on Monday (September 7, 2026) remanded Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to 14 days in judicial custody in connection with the alleged assault of the father of a student during a protest at Jantar Mantar in July organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of the Patiala House Courts passed the order after Mr. Bhardwaj was produced before the court following the completion of his one-day police custody.
The court had remanded him to police custody for a day on Saturday (September 5). He will be produced before the court again on September 21.
Mr. Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, on Friday (September 4), a few hours after the CJP held a demonstration outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest in connection with the alleged assault.
The Delhi police subsequently added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR registered against Mr. Bhardwaj over the alleged assault of the minor activist’s father. A separate case under the POCSO Act has also been registered against him.
Mr. Bhardwaj came under scrutiny after a video podcast in which he claimed to have “cracked the skull” of the student’s father during the demonstration went viral. He also claimed during the interview that he had political connections that helped him avoid arrest.

briefs.headline: Balance needed between scientific probe and right to privacy, says SC
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said technological advancements have made criminal investigation far more complicated and a challenge for the investigating agencies, as they get the stick from the court and the victim for not conducting the probe scientifically, and on the other hand, are accused of violation of privacy if they do.
“A balance needs to be struck,” said a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, while dealing with an application by journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, who claimed to be whistleblower on pilferage of Ram temple donations, and has accused Ghaziabad police of making an FIR in an alleged road rage case the pretext for seeking his digital footprints from June 1 from social media platforms to find his sources.

briefs.headline: Bolivia confirms 9 deaths after military base explosion
briefs.deck: Army Commander Hector Alarcón said an even greater tragedy was averted because many personnel from the Bolivar Regiment were away on a recreational bicycle ride when the explosion occurred.
briefs.bodyText:
Bolivian authorities on Monday (September 7, 2026) confirmed that nine people have died following an explosion at a military barracks in the municipality of Viacha, about 30 km from La Paz, on Friday (September 4).
The Defence Ministry said a ninth body was recovered from the rubble on Monday afternoon and transferred to the morgue for identification. Army Commander Hector Alarcón said an even greater tragedy was averted because many personnel from the Bolivar Regiment were away on a recreational bicycle ride when the explosion occurred.
Authorities did not say how many people remain missing. “Our priority remains finding our comrades who are still missing and providing answers to their families as soon as possible,” Mr. Alarcón said at a press conference earlier on Monday.
Health Minister Marcela Flores said 84 people had been treated since Friday’s blast, with 31 still hospitalised. President Rodrigo Paz said the cause of the explosion was under investigation, but it appeared to have been an accident caused by the improper handling of explosives stored at the military facility.
“Our Armed Forces are reviewing their protocols and everything needed to provide greater safety, not only for enlisted personnel and officers, but also for nearby residents living close to military bases,” Paz said. He also announced a period of national mourning and urged people not to politicise the tragedy.
The blast occurred at around 2.30 p.m. on Friday in an area used to store pyrotechnic material, authorities said.

briefs.headline: Iran values long-standing, civilisational ties with India: Foreign Ministry
briefs.deck: Just days before the BRICS summit, Mr. Baghaei said that Chabahar Port is one of the issues of bilateral talks between India and Iran. He said, “Various issues are usually discussed during consultations between Iran and India, including the Chabahar Port, which is important to both countries.”
briefs.bodyText:
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Iran shares a long-standing, historic and civilisational relationship with India and attaches great importance to its ties with the country.
On Tuesday (September 8, 2026), the Iranian Embassy in India released a statement from Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson where he said, referring to the recent meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan’s capital, Bishkek, that “President Masoud Pezeshkian met with the Indian Prime Minister in Bishkek. Our relationship with India is built on long-standing civilisational and historic ties, and we highly value our partnership.”
In the first top-level meeting between Iran and India since the beginning of the war on Iran this February, Mr. Modi on August 31 met Mr. Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan’s capital Bishkek and urged him to ensure peace and stability in West Asia and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Talking about the 18th BRICS Summit, Mr. Baghaei said, “We will certainly make use of the opportunity provided by the BRICS Summit to continue our discussions and consultations with India in areas of mutual interest.”
Just days before the BRICS summit, Mr. Baghaei also said that Chabahar Port is one of the issues of bilateral talks between India and Iran. He said, “Various issues are usually discussed during consultations between Iran and India, including the Chabahar Port, which is important to both countries.”
The Chabahar port is being developed by India and Iran to boost connectivity and trade ties. Both countries are also strongly pitching for making Chabahar port an integral part of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).
Chabahar provides India with direct access to Afghanistan, bypassing Pakistan, which denies India land transit routes. It enhances India’s trade routes and reduces dependence on traditional maritime chokepoints.
India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The summit will bring together leaders of BRICS member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.

briefs.headline: U.K. recognises India's carbon credit scheme under its carbon tax mechanism: official
briefs.deck: With this recognition, U.K. importers of eligible Indian goods covered under CBAM will be able to seek carbon price relief
briefs.bodyText:
In a major breakthrough, the U.K. has recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as a qualifying criterion for pricing relief under its carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), a move that would reduce the tax burden on domestic exporters, an official said on Monday (September 7, 2026).
In a communication addressed to the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, the U.K.'s HM Treasury confirmed that the CCTS has been included in the U.K.'s published indicative list of overseas carbon pricing schemes assessed as qualifying criteria under a provision of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Calculation of CBAM Rate and Determination of Carbon Price Relief) Regulations 2026, the official said.
The move is important as the Commerce Ministry was pursuing the matter with the U.K. for long.
The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has been notified by India with the objective of reducing, removing, or avoiding greenhouse gas emissions from the Indian economy by pricing such emissions through the trading of Carbon Credit Certificates.
The financial support for implementation of the CCTS would be met by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency from fees and charges collected from entities under the scheme and its own resources.
The official said the U.K. government had included the scheme in its indicative list as a qualifying carbon pricing mechanism under Britain's CBAM.
With this recognition, U.K. importers of eligible Indian goods covered under CBAM will be able to seek carbon price relief corresponding to the effective carbon price borne by those goods under the CCTS, subject to satisfying the evidence and verification requirements prescribed under U.K. law.
"This will reduce the effective CBAM liability on Indian goods, directly benefiting Indian exporters to the U.K.," the official said.
The recognition follows sustained technical-level engagement between the two governments on the design and implementation of the CCTS.
The recognition reflects the U.K. CBAM's core principle of avoiding double taxation on goods that have already borne an eligible carbon price in their country of origin.
Going forward, cooperation on carbon market design and implementation will continue through the U.K.-India Energy Memorandum of Understanding and the Partnership for Market Implementation.
The two governments are also committed to continued dialogue on carbon pricing, including on the interaction between the CCTS and U.K. CBAM rules, further strengthening India-U.K. engagement.
However, the amount of relief that can be claimed will depend on the effective carbon price to which the goods in question have been subject.
A liable person for U.K. CBAM will still be required to satisfy the applicable evidence and verification requirements.
India and the U.K. have implemented a comprehensive economic and trade partnership on July 15.
Merchandise trade between the two countries stood at $25.1 billion in 2025-26, while bilateral services trade reached $35.4 billion in 2024.

stories.headline: At 31.9°C, Bengaluru closer to 75-year September heat record
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 By its traditional weather calendar, Bengaluru should now be basking in one of the southwest monsoon’s wettest phases. Instead, temperatures in Bengaluru are hovering between 30°C and 32°C for the past few days, pushing the city perilously close to a 75-year Sept heat record.
According to India Meteorological Department, Bengaluru touched 32.2°C on Sunday, followed by 31.9°C on Monday, unusual for September.
Bengaluru’s all-time Sept maximum is 33.3°C, recorded on Sept 16, 1951. Monday’s maximum was 1.4°C short of that mark. “The near-record temperature across Bengaluru city is largely influenced by El Nino. This dry condition is likely to prevail for the next couple of days,” said CS Patil, scientist at IMD, Bengaluru.
The heat is accompanied by an equally unusual absence of rain across large parts of the state. While some parts of north 
Karnataka
 received light to moderate isolated showers, coastal Karnataka and south-interior Karnataka recorded nil rainfall. A senior official from Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre said as many as 122 taluks had reported zero rainfall for three consecutive weeks.
With Karnataka declaring 101 of its 239 taluks as drought-hit, officials expect the number to rise sharply before the official southwest monsoon season ends later this month. The prolonged dry spell has disrupted the state’s kharif-sowing pattern. Agriculture and horticulture officials said the impact is beginning to show across rainfed areas, with production expected to take a major hit.

stories.headline: Students marginalised in Bengaluru while schools occupied for Special Intensive Revision
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Until last Thursday, a day at this private school in the city followed its usual rhythm — classrooms filled with lessons, children heading out for lunch, and teachers going about their routines. Since then, however, the campus has taken on an entirely different character — Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials have occupied the premises for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work, leaving the school teeming with members of the public.
“We have a small campus. Our children have lunch outside the classrooms, on the stage. That is where the public is meeting with officials. Where will our children go? There has been so much noise on the campus that teachers are unable to teach and students are unable to focus in classrooms. We’re also worried about the safety and security of children, with strangers loitering around,” said the school’s headmistress.
The school has 650 students, of whom 36 have special needs. “There are autistic, specially abled, and deaf and mute students in the group. They get anxious with the commotion around. We requested that SIR be conducted after school hours or on weekends, but officials told us that this might go on for the next two months,” she said.
The school has now written to the 
election commission
 that the SIR work be conducted during non-school hours.
Several other private, aided, and govt schools are in a similar fix. “SIR hearings began in our school on Sept 5. There are 12 booth-level officers sitting here. Around 50 people come to meet each BLO every day. Our school has four rooms, of which three are occupied by these officials. All our students — around 60 of them — are seated in the office room. This will go on till Oct 22,” said a teacher at a govt school in east Bengaluru.
TOI
 has highlighted in the past the plight of several teachers recruited for SIR work.
School associations have slammed the state govt for ignoring the needs of schools. “On one hand, there are no teachers available for teaching, and on the other, school infrastructure is being hijacked for other work. For elections, schools were taken over for 1-2 days by govt. Now, they are being taken over for months altogether,” said D Shashi Kumar, secretary of the Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools of Karnataka.

stories.headline: Bengaluru gets Circular Textile Lab to keep fabric waste out of landfills
stories.bodyText:
To keep textile waste out of landfills and create employment opportunities for local tailors and women, Bengaluru’s first Circular Textile Lab was inaugurated at Kasa Rasa Kendra, a ward-level solid waste management centre initiated by the NGO Saahas, in Koramangala on Monday. This is the first such initiative in the city.
The facility, an initiative by South City Corporation, was inaugurated by Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy, alongside other GBA officials.
The Circular Textile Lab will collect textile waste from garment units and tailors and process it for reuse. The facility will use the collected material to make garments and eco-friendly bags, while providing employment opportunities to economically-disadvantaged communities.
A thrift store is also being set up at the facility to sell products made from recycled textiles. The revenue generated will be used for the welfare of workers and management of the project. The centre also has an effluent and sewage treatment system to treat dyes and chemicals generated during textile processing.
The project, which has previously been implemented in the Kolar Gold Fields (KGF), will initially operate in Koramangala and will expand to other wards in Bengaluru.
Alongside the textile lab, an SWM Learning Centre was also inaugurated at the Kasa Rasa Kendra. The center will offer training on waste segregation, composting, waste reduction at source and the 7 R principles of sustainability that expands the traditional 3 R’s (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) into a comprehensive framework that prioritises waste prevention over disposal.
Unlike an usual classroom-based training facility, the centre is located within an operational waste-processing unit that handles around 18 tonnes of waste a day. The public will be able to use the facility for hands-on learning about waste management.

stories.headline: Over 3,300 breakdowns on three flyovers in 19 months: Why Bengaluru is putting restrictions on goods vehicles
stories.deck: The Peenya flyover witnessed a total of 1,126 breakdown incidents, while the airport road flyover reported 1,100, and the B.G.S. flyover on Mysuru Road witnessed 1,090 incidents
stories.bodyText:
Three of the five elevated corridors in Bengaluru, on which goods vehicles, trucks and heavy vehicles are banned, witnessed 1,000-plus incidents each of goods vehicle breakdowns in 19 months between 2025 and 2026 (July), according to official data accessed by The Hindu.
The Peenya flyover witnessed a total of 1,126 breakdown incidents, while the airport road flyover reported 1,100, and the B.G.S. flyover on Mysuru Road witnessed 1,090 incidents. The Electronics City and Double Decker flyovers witnessed 398 and 271 incidents, respectively, the data revealed.
The breakdown incidents include heavy vehicles, light goods vehicles, and smaller trucks, as per the Bengaluru Traffic Police classification. Restrictions on these flyovers have been in effect since September 4 on all flyovers, barring the Electronics City elevated corridor, where the restriction will begin on September 11.
Increase in goods vehicles entering city
According to the data, barring the airport road corridor, the flyovers are witnessing a spike in the number of breakdowns every year. For example, on the B.G.S. flyover, nearly 300 incidents of goods vehicle breakdowns were reported in the first seven months, while in the corresponding period of 2026, the flyover has witnessed 503 breakdowns.
A senior police officer explained that the trend of increase in numbers has been witnessed for many years now. In some cases, there has been an uptick in breakdown incidents for over a decade, which became the reason for the police to impose restrictions.
“Goods vehicles entering the city have increased multifold in the last decade, along with the booming industries and commercial activities in the city. This increase has had a negative impact on traffic in terms of slowing down the commute speed, which results in an increase in commute time as well,” the officer said.
“If such big vehicles break down on corridors like the airport stretch, traffic in an entire part of the city is paralysed. So, restrictions have been planned,” he explained.
Impact on traffic movement
The officer explained that a breakdown on an elevated corridor will have an immediate impact on traffic, as the limited carriageway leaves little room for motorists to manoeuvre around a stranded vehicle.
“During breakdowns, suddenly there is a queue of vehicles behind the stranded vehicle. Many times, this queue spills over to ramps as well. So, there is a larger impact, which cannot be managed without traffic personnel. In case it happens somewhere in the middle of the corridor, it will be difficult for even police personnel to reach the spot,” he explained.
He pointed out that some flyovers have witnessed two breakdowns in a day, and many times, they occurred during peak hours. “Even one breakdown will take nearly three to four hours to clear if it’s in the middle of the corridor. In addition, we need towing vehicles to reach the location, which further slows down the traffic,” he added.
Further, the officer stressed that goods vehicles are not banned entirely on elevated corridors. There is a time adjustment, especially keeping peak hours in mind, while there is no impact on commercial activities as well.
Karthik Reddy, Joint Commissioner (Traffic), said that before the restrictions were planned, a comprehensive survey was taken up to assess the impact and outcome, and based on those results, the restrictions have been imposed.
While commuters welcome the move, they still question the logic behind the ban on two-wheelers, stressing that flyovers are not only for car owners but for all sections of society. However, police maintain that the restrictions are for the safety of two-wheeler riders.

briefs.headline: 1.4 lakh tonnes of construction and demolition waste cleared in Bengaluru in August 2026
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and other govt agencies cleared 1,40,277 tonnes of construction and demolition (C&D) waste across Bengaluru in Aug as part of the ‘Freedom from Waste–Just Clean Bengaluru’ campaign, according to GBA data.
Launched on Aug 1, the month-long campaign focused on clearing accumulated construction debris, soil, discarded materials and other waste dumped along roadsides, footpaths, vacant sites and other public spaces. GBA had identified 1,54,073 tonnes of C&D waste across the city’s five corporations. Of this, the five corporations together cleared and transported 82,125 tonnes during the campaign. The cleared waste was transported to five designated disposal locations, including dysfunctional quarries, for disposal.
Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the reclaimed spaces would be protected and used only for public purposes. “Our first priority is to safeguard the spaces that have been reclaimed after debris clearance. We will plan as per local needs,” he said.
The state govt has also announced measures to curb fresh dumping of C&D waste. These include registration and GPS tracking of vehicles transporting the waste.

briefs.headline: Fridge technician molests woman at Bengaluru home, beaten up
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A home appliance service turned frightening for a 23-year-old woman in southeast Bengaluru as a man claiming to be a technician allegedly molested her while repairing her refrigerator at her home.
In her complaint, 
Sneha
 (name changed) said she had contacted the customer care of a home appliance firm by dialling a phone number she found on the internet on Sept 3 to get her refrigerator repaired. She was reportedly told that a technician would visit her home.
Accordingly, a man arrived and introduced himself as the company’s technician.
Sneha told police that he started the repair work and asked her to assist him in picking or holding the materials. While she was assisting him, the technician allegedly touched her inappropriately and spoke to her objectionably.
As a shocked Sneha shouted at him, he stopped the work and left the house.
After her husband returned home from work, the duo discussed the matter and planned to call the technician the next day.
He readily agreed to complete the work and visited her home on Sept 4. As he tried to misbehave again, Sneha’s husband and neighbours confronted him. 
He was beaten up but he managed to escape.
Begur police registered a case of sexual harassment. A senior officer said, “We have traced the accused and have served him a notice for further investigation. The offence is punishable with less than seven years, so we cannot arrest him and produce before the court. We will be filing a report to the court based on the evidence.”

briefs.headline: Brothel customer gets bail in Pocso case in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court has granted bail to a 25-year-old man from Karkala in Udupi district, observing that as a customer of a brothel, it could not have been possible for him to know the actual age and caste of the survivor.
Justice S Rachaiah made the observation in an order passed on Aug 10 while allowing the man’s petition. The court directed him to furnish a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh and appear before the trial court on all hearing dates. He was also directed not to commit any similar offence or threaten any prosecution witnesses.
Between Dec 24 and 26, 2025, the girl in question was allegedly kept at a house in Mangaluru and told to cooperate with “customers”. Her father was also allegedly involved. On returning to Birur, she informed her uncle and aunt, who lodged a complaint under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act, 2012, Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, Juvenile Justice Act, 1986, and the SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015.
Following registration of the case, the petitioner was arrested. A sessions court rejected his bail plea on March 25, following which he approached the high court. The petitioner, arraigned as accused no. 2, claimed he was merely a customer and was unaware of the survivor’s age. He also claimed he did not know that she belonged to an SC community.

briefs.headline: SIR: Amid pressure, Karnataka CEO makes SIR notice list public
briefs.deck: A total of 43.81 lakh people across the State have been marked to receive notices
briefs.bodyText:
After sustained public pressure, with several people reporting that they had received notices at the last minute, leaving them with a narrow window to respond, the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) has made the notice list public.
A total of 43.81 lakh people across the State have been marked to receive notices.
The list can be accessed here: https://ceo.karnataka.gov.in/notices_issued.html
But, there is a problem: It does not specify the hearing venue, date or time. This leaves voters in the dark about when and where they are expected to appear, adding to the confusion and burden surrounding an already opaque process.
With hearings having begun on Thursday across Karnataka, the situation has left many people with no option but to miss their hearings because of the short notice and lack of prior information. The public can now access the list, with district-wise files uploaded on the website, similar to the ASDDO list.
The major hurdle flagged by electors is that only the person issued the notice can appear for the hearing, and no one else can represent the voter at the hearing venue. Moreover, a hearing can be rescheduled only once, at the discretion of the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO).
Electors have also flagged that Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are not visiting voters’ homes to serve notices, but are instead asking them to collect the notices from the polling station, citing their duties at hearing venues. However, the hearings are to be conducted by the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), not the BLOs.
Notices have been issued for two broad reasons: non-mapping, where a voter could not map their own or their parent’s details to the 2002 electoral rolls, and anomalies or “logical discrepancies”, such as an implausible age gap between an elector and their parents or grandparents, differences in the spelling of the father’s name, or a mismatch in the voter’s own name in cases of self-mapping.
However, while these are the stated reasons for generating notices, several people in Bengaluru have reported receiving notices despite having filled in all their details correctly.
Even where a voter has correctly provided all the required details and there is no actual logical discrepancy or mapping gap, being wrongly issued a notice does not spare them the inquiry. Recently, in Byatarayanapura, the Bengaluru DEO found that three people had been issued notices despite the mapping details they had provided being correct. Yet, the order still required them to appear for an inquiry. The entire burden continues to fall on the voter, even when the error is not theirs.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru firm Pixxel raises $100 million to build infrastructure for a changing planet
briefs.deck: The funding will accelerate Pixxel’s expansion beyond hyperspectral imaging as it builds planetary infrastructure spanning advanced sensing satellites, earth intelligence software, sovereign space systems, and satellite manufacturing
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru-based planetary infrastructure company Pixxel on September 7 announced the close of its $100 million Series C funding round, co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, with participation from new investors 360 ONE Asset, IMM Investment, and existing investors Radical Ventures, and growX ventures. This round brings Pixxel’s total funding to $195 million.
According to the firm, the investment marked the single largest funding round by a space technology company in India, and signalled the company’s next phase of growth as it broadens its role across the space-tech value chain.
Pixxel began with hyperspectral satellites that could reveal information about the Earth’s surface beyond what conventional imagery could capture. Since then, the company has expanded its scope to include Aurora, its Earth intelligence software, and satellite systems for both commercial and sovereign space missions.
Together, these form the core of Pixxel’s planetary infrastructure vision, connecting sensors, software, and space systems to help governments, industries, and institutions turn Earth observation into actionable intelligence.
Awais Ahmed, founder and CEO of Pixxel, said, “Years ago, we set out to build a health monitor for the planet. Hyperspectral imaging gave us a fundamentally new way to see Earth. This new investment gives us the scale to turn that vision into planetary infrastructure.”
More ways of sensing, more intelligence from every image, and more sovereign capability for nations, Mr. Ahmed said adding, “Our goal is to make a changing planet understandable in time to act.”
Mark Boggett, CEO at Seraphim Space, said, “Pixxel is exceptionally well-positioned across some of the most important themes shaping the future of the space sector, from AI-powered Earth observation and sovereign space capabilities to the rise of India as a global SpaceTech leader. We’re delighted to deepen our support as the company continues to scale.”
The Series C funding is expected to accelerate four strategic priorities: Pixxel would extend its sensing capabilities through the Honeybee constellation, high-resolution optical imaging satellites, and other technologies, while further developing Aurora as the intelligence layer that combines these datasets into decision-ready insights.
The company would deepen its work on sovereign Earth observation systems and accelerate its manufacturing capacity through Gigapixxel, its next-generation facility designed for high-rate production of advanced satellites.
Over the past two years, Pixxel has deployed six Firefly satellites, forming the world’s highest-resolution commercial hyperspectral constellation, and launched Aurora, its Earth intelligence software platform. The company has secured contracts with NASA and the NRO, won multiple iDEX challenges of the Indian Ministry of Defence, unveiled plans for an orbital data-centre demonstration satellite, and has been selected to lead the development of India’s first public-private Earth observation constellation of 12 satellites under IN-SPACe, according to the company.
With the new funding, these efforts would further Pixxel’s goal of building the infrastructure needed to deliver intelligence for a changing planet.

briefs.headline: Karnataka files appeal before CWMA seeking reduction in water release
briefs.deck: Appeal comes ahead of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee meeting scheduled on September 8
briefs.bodyText:
Ahead of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) meeting scheduled this week, Karnataka has filed an appeal before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) seeking a reduction in water release to Tamil Nadu from 9,000 cusecs a day, as ordered by it, to 2,000 cusecs.
It may be noted that the CWMA had upheld the CWRC’s August 25 direction to Karnataka, asking it to ensure flows of 9,000 cusecs a day for 15 days from August 25 to be realised at the Biligundlu water gauge on the inter-State border. According to the CWMA’s order, the releases by Karnataka would total up to 11.66 tmcft.
The CWRC is meeting again on September 8 to review the ground-level situation. On the same day, the CWMA is also meeting to review the situation.
Meanwhile, Karnataka has filed an appeal before the CWMA seeking a reduction in water release on the grounds that the inflows into its Cauvery reservoirs are very low. It has also pointed out that the southwest Monsoon is set to end soon, indicating that there is no hope for the State that there will be further inflows into its Cauvery reservoirs in the future.
It may be noted that Karnataka, on August 25, had appealed to the CWMA to adopt a cautious approach while asking for any further release, and requested the Authority to reassess the situation after observing the forthcoming northeast monsoon. The State had told the CWMA that its Cauvery basin area was facing severe hydrological distress, due to which cumulative inflows into its four reservoirs in the Cauvery basin were about 49.18% below the 30-year average.

stories.headline: Swiggy swaps retail platform Lynk for 3.2% Udaan stake
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Swiggy is selling its retail distribution platform Lynk Logistics to B2B e-commerce startup Udaan, the companies said on Monday. As part of the deal, which has been structured as a share-swap transaction, Swiggy will acquire a 2.8% stake in Udaan.
The food and grocery delivery major will also make a cash infusion of Rs 75 crore in the company, buying an additional 0.4% stake, taking its total shareholding in Udaan to 3.2%. The deal will value Lynk at Rs 500 crore.
The development comes less than two months after Udaan struck a $160 million financing deal with existing and new investors, averting bankruptcy. Global creditors of the company had initiated insolvency proceedings against Udaan's Singapore-based parent over a $170 million bond default. The startup, which plans to go public, claimed that the recapitalisation has boosted its balance sheet and it has achieved EBITDA profitability in its largest operating city, Bengaluru.
"Bringing Lynk together with Udaan combines complementary capabilities with Udaan's scale and technology-led platform serving India's retail ecosystem," said Rahul Bothra, CFO at Swiggy.
Founded in 2015, Lynk was acquired by Swiggy through a share swap deal with Chennai-based Ramco Group in 2023.
Udaan said the acquisition will strengthen its distribution platform and allow the firm to connect consumer brands with a wider network of retailers. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kolkata collectively contribute nearly 75% of Lynk's revenues, giving Udaan deeper access to key markets.

stories.headline: Blackstone in fray to acquire IIFL Fin stake
stories.deck: Deal To Help Fairfax Comply With Law As It Eyes IDBI Bk
stories.bodyText:
Blackstone Inc is among global investment firms in the fray to buy a stake in IIFL Finance, just as Fairfax Financial Holdings looks to exit from the company, according to people familiar with the matter.
Fairfax, founded by Indian-born Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, is weighing selling its entire holding in IIFL Finance to comply with regulatory guidelines as it inches towards acquiring 
IDBI Bank
, said the people, asking not to be named discussing private matters. The plans for IIFL Finance are preliminary and could be subject to change, they added.
Blackstone is in talks with Fairfax and other shareholders to acquire the stake in IIFL Finance, the people said. The private equity firm's potential involvement comes at a time when India's financial services industry has become a target for acquisitions. Last year, the US alternative investment manager invested more than $700 million for a 9.9% stake in Federal Bank.
Fairfax and IIFL Finance did not immediately respond to separate requests for comment. Blackstone declined to respond.
Fairfax held a 15.2% stake in IIFL Finance as of June 30, according to data compiled by Bloomberg, with the Indian firm having a market value of $2.9 billion. 
The stock erased gains of as much as 2.4% to trade 1.2% lower on Monday.
Fairfax's move underscores how it is gearing up to acquire a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank in a sweetened offer that Indian authorities are close to accepting, people have previously said. A successful bid for the Mumbai-based lender could be valued at $6.2 billion at current prices, potentially making it the biggest foreign investment in the country's banking sector.
Buyers are drawn by the growing flow of household savings into formal investments, rising credit demand and the opportunity to scale in a rapidly digitising market, though regulations often complicate deals.
If Fairfax acquires IDBI Bank, it is expected to consolidate some of its existing Indian investments in lending firms in line with regulatory rules, according to the people. Fairfax also owns a 40% stake in small private-sector lender CSB Bank.
(This is a Bloomberg story)

stories.headline: JLR to cut 4,000 jobs in two years to save £1.7 billion
stories.deck: “The reduction, which is not expected to impact direct manufacturing jobs, will be achieved through voluntary means wherever possible,” TMPV said in an exchange filing
stories.bodyText:
Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPV), as part of its “strategic transformation programme,” has announced to reduce its global workforce by around 4,000 roles over the next two years.
“The reduction, which is not expected to impact direct manufacturing jobs, will be achieved through voluntary means wherever possible,” TMPV said in an exchange filing.
“JLR is today [September 7, 2026] beginning consultation on the first round of reductions and will provide support to all colleagues affected by the changes and engage with Trade Unions and employee representatives throughout the transition,” the statement added.
PB Balaji, CEO, JLR, in a statement, said, “We recognise this will be difficult news for colleagues affected, and are committed to supporting everyone with care, fairness and respect.”
JLR said the “strategic transformation programme” is designed to “simplify the organisation, improve operational performance and support long-term sustainable growth.”
“As per JLR’s “Growth Reimagined” strategy announced at its Investor Day on 19 June 2026, JLR is targeting approximately £1.7 billion of savings over the next two years to reduce its break-evens towards 300,000 units,” the company said.
The savings are designed to enhance JLR’s ability to deliver sustainable profitable growth, against the backdrop of an increasingly competitive and rapidly changing markets and continuing geo-political uncertainty, it added.
“The programme will reduce organisational complexity, and underpin the commitment to invest between £15-18 billion in electrification, digital technologies, advanced manufacturing and enhanced customer experiences over the next 5 years,” Mr Balaji said.
“The automotive industry faces significant challenges, with technological change amidst intense competition and ongoing geo-political uncertainty. Through our Growth Reimagined strategy, JLR is moving decisively to strengthen our competitiveness and position the business for long-term success,” he said.
Over the next 12 months, the company will launch five new products, continue to leverage the strength of its brands and renew its focus on North America, amongst other markets, to help it deliver double digit revenue growth, he stated.

stories.headline: RBL Bank to raise to $1 billion from overseas investors
stories.deck: The board approved the establishment of an EMTN Programme in accordance with Regulation S of the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, subject to regulatory, statutory, and other approvals, RBL Bank said in a stock exchange filing
stories.bodyText:
Private lender RBL Bank on Monday (September 7, 2026) said its board approved the mobilisation of up to $1 billion from overseas investors through bond issuance.
The board approved the establishment of a Euro Medium Term Note Programme (EMTN Programme) in accordance with Regulation S of the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, subject to regulatory, statutory, and other approvals, RBL Bank said in a stock exchange filing.
The board cleared a proposal to enable issuance of foreign currency bonds/notes/any other debt securities up to $1 billion in the future, from time to time, through one or more transactions, subject to the market conditions and regulatory compliances, for raising funds through permissible modes under the EMTN Programme, the bank said.
The private lender informed the stock exchanges that the board also gave the go-ahead to delegate certain powers and authorities to the bank's Borrowing Committee to decide and undertake all necessary actions in connection with the EMTN Programme and the issuance of the securities.
In June, Emirates NBD Bank announced the successful completion of the acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank through a primary infusion of approximately $2.75 billion (about ₹26,000 crore).
It constitutes the largest foreign direct investment in the Indian banking sector, the largest equity fund raise in the Indian banking sector, one of the largest fund raises through preferential issuance by a listed company in India and marks the first acquisition of a majority interest in a profitable Indian bank by a foreign bank.
The investment has been completed through a preferential issue of shares, resulting in Emirates NBD acquiring a majority stake in RBL Bank.
In connection with the transaction, Emirates NBD also completed a mandatory open offer to the public shareholders of RBL Bank in accordance with applicable regulations. Following the completion of the transaction, Emirates NBD holds 60% of the expanded share capital of RBL Bank.

briefs.headline: We'll make Air India great again: Gebremariam
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: "Focus on safety, financial stability, winning trust of passengers and offer a consistent customer experience." 
Tata Sons
 and 
Air India
 chairman N Chandrasekaran Monday set the objectives for the airline and its new boss in a town hall with the carrier's outgoing and incoming MDs and CEOs Campbell Wilson and Tewolde Gebremariam, respectively. Taking a leaf from Trump's MAGA, Gebremariam promised to "make Air India great again" as the airline tries to come out of some serious turbulence.
To Focus On Safety, Operational Execution, Customer Trust & Cost Discipline: Chandra
Chandra acknowledged that the last 18 months had been particularly challenging for the airline due to geopolitical disruptions, airspace closures, fuel volatility and the deadly Ahmedabad crash. "For me, bringing Air India back to the Tata Group is one of the most important milestones of my career... AI belongs to a billion people.... It is probably the only business that a billion people talk about, have views on, criticise fiercely and appreciate at times.... all these one billion people are rooting for AI. That is our biggest strength," said Chandra, who has announced he is not going to seek a fresh term as Tata boss next Feb.
The "next phase" of AI will focus on safety, customer trust, operational execution and cost discipline. 
"The most important thing Air India should aspire to have is trust in the minds of people. AI must be known for caring about safety above everything else. Our safety record should not just match the best airlines in the world, it should be better than the best," he said.
Given AI's mounting losses in a tough operating environment and a bloated cost structure, Chandra urged employees to help build a stronger culture of cost consciousness so that the airline becomes financially sustainable. "Every individual in Air India can contribute to improving cost efficiency."
Gebremariam, who is credited with turning around Ethiopian Airlines group during his long stint there, will take over as AI MD and CEO after getting the required security clearance. Setting his priorities, he has set sight on fixing the basics first with safety at the top. "A safety-first culture has to be our number one priority. It is not enough to say it. We must live it every day. If something is not right, stop. Every employee should feel empowered to raise concerns, and I will support that culture."
"Operational excellence is about getting the basics right every day: On-time departures, on-time arrivals, baggage delivery and clean aircraft. Customer experience is a function of operational excellence. We need to minimise disruptions and when they do occur, handle them professionally and take care of our customers," Gebremariam said. Seeking employees' support in turning around AI, he said: "We cannot bring about meaningful change without the commitment of our people. Together, we can build a safer, stronger and truly world class AI."
Noting the progress made in last four years, outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson said: "I would like to acknowledge all Air Indians whose commitment, resilience and hard work have made this transformation possible. As the chairman said, this is a task that is not yet complete. The transformation will continue, and Air India's best days are still ahead."

briefs.headline: 6-week high: India's crude import price hits $100-a-barrel mark
briefs.deck: Likely To Rise Further Amid West Asia Crisis
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's average crude import price crossed the $100 per barrel mark for the first time in six weeks last Friday and is likely to rise further as international crude prices surge amid intensified hostilities in West Asia and supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.
Indian basket of crude oil - derived average of the sweet-grade global benchmark Dated Brent and the sour-grade benchmarks of Oman and Dubai - increased to $101.07 per barrel Friday, the highest since July 23, Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell data showed.
Likely To Rise Further Amid West Asia Crisis
Along with crude, international free-on-board (FOB) prices of petrol and diesel have also surged. While the international FOB price of diesel has averaged $156.88 a barrel this month, up from $149.35 in Aug, the corresponding price for petrol has averaged $122.12 this month, compared to $110.87 in Aug. Premium on diesel over crude has narrowed to 55% from 70% in the last 10 days. The crude basket has so far averaged $99.38 per barrel in Sept, up from $90.19 in Aug. It was above $100 per barrel during the peak of the conflict in March, April and May.
An oil company executive said this could lead to higher under-recoveries for oil marketing companies (OMCs) if prices remain elevated for a longer duration and retail pump prices remain unchanged.
Oil retailers were making an under-recovery of more than Rs 1,000 crore a day during the peak of the conflict in May, when the Indian basket of crude oil averaged more than $110 per barrel.
Ratings agency ICRA said renewed hostilities between Iran and the US pose a challenge for the limited crude oil supplies coming through the Strait of Hormuz. "As Iran threatens to establish a new restricted maritime zone extending beyond the Strait of Hormuz, additional energy flows beyond the latter could be at risk. Owing to these developments, crude oil prices have increased in the past few days, and the Indian crude basket has crossed the $100/barrel mark," said Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president and co-group head, corporate ratings, ICRA.

briefs.headline: Surplus liquidity: RBI mops up ₹6 lakh crore in two auctions with mixed response
briefs.deck: As against ₹7 lakh crore of notified amount, the first auction received a tepid response, with bids of just over ₹2.59 lakh crore being received for the 30-day VRRR, according to an official statement
briefs.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India on Monday (September 7, 2026) mopped up over ₹6 lakh crore of excess funds from the banking system in two auctions, which saw an underwhelming response from banks despite surplus liquidity.
The 30-day variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auction announced last week received a tepid response from banks, and the central bank announced another auction in the first half of the day.
As against ₹7 lakh crore of notified amount, the first auction received a tepid response, with bids of just over ₹2.59 lakh crore being received for the 30-day VRRR, according to an official statement.
The bids for the 30-day VRRR were accepted at the cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24%, according to the RBI.
Soon afterwards, the RBI announced an overnight VRRR auction with a notified amount of ₹5 lakh crore, which was completed at 11:30 hrs.
Market response to the second auction was a tad better, with bids of ₹3,53,390 crore received, which amounts to over 70% of the notified amount, indicating that lenders are comfortable parking funds for a shorter tenure.
For the overnight, the RBI accepted the full amount at a cut-off rate and weighted average rate of 5.24%. A VRRR auction is a monetary policy tool used by a central bank to absorb excess cash from the banking system.
Liquidity in the banking system was estimated to be in surplus of around ₹11.16 lakh crore as on September 6.
The RBI has stepped up liquidity absorption operations as the banking system has been flooded with funds following large inflows through the special FCNR(B) deposit scheme.
The RBI's special forex measures mobilised $136.38 billion by August 31, including $127.23 billion through FCNR(B) deposits, $5.26 billion through OFCBs, and $3.89 billion through ECBs, according to RBI data.
The FCNR(B) window was closed a month early on August 31 due to the strong response, while the ECB/OFCB facility remains open till December 31 and inflows through these routes are expected to pick up.
The mobilisation brought foreign currency into the banking system, while subsequent swaps with the RBI provided banks with rupee liquidity.
To align with the repo rate, the Central Bank has conducted 32 VRRR auctions between August and so far in September, with maturities ranging from overnight to 14 days.

briefs.headline: Govt spurs coal rake loading by 20% to strengthen stocks positions at thermal plants
briefs.deck: CEA data indicates 53 domestic coal-fired plants were operating with less than 25% of their critical normative requirements as on September 5
briefs.bodyText:
Loading of coal rakes for supply to the power sector has grown about 20% between September 3 and September 6, the Union Coal Ministry said on Monday (September 7, 2026), adding separately that it was also closely monitoring thermal plants with stocks below 25% of their normal requirements with measures being taken to ease their supply position.
According to data from the Central Electricity Authority, 53 domestic coal-fired plants were operating at the critical normative level as on September 5.
“The number of critical thermal plants [stock below 25% of normative requirement] are being closely monitored, with corrective coal supply measures already in place to further ease the position at these plants,” it stated.
On the increased rake loading, the Ministry stated that coal loading to the power sector has increased from 370 rakes in a day on September 3, to 387 rakes the day after, 413 rakes September 5 and 444 rakes on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
Further, the government informed that state-owned Coal India’s daily coal production has accelerated about 35% to about 1.83 million tonnes on September 6 – compared to the first three days of the month.
“The improvement comes as mining conditions steadily recover and affected transportation routes and working areas are restored,” the ministry observed.
It added that average daily despatch to the power sector has also increased 24% to 1.7 MT during the same period.

briefs.headline: Salary stayed Rs 2.6 lakh after maternity leave, but duties were cut; HC awards Rs 10 lakh
briefs.deck: The High Court has made it clear that the statutory safeguard also covers the work she performs, her position in the organisational hierarchy, supervisory powers and opportunities for appraisal and promotion.
briefs.bodyText:
A woman with 14 years’ experience returned to her job after maternity leave only to find that while her salary had remained the same, her managerial duties had been reduced. Now the 
Delhi High Court
 has ruled that maternity protection cannot be treated as a matter of simply preserving a woman employee's salary and job title.
The High Court has made it clear that the statutory safeguard also covers the work she performs, her position in the organisational hierarchy, supervisory powers and opportunities for appraisal and promotion.
Justice Sachin Datta, in a judgment delivered on August 31, 2026, said a woman who returns to work after maternity leave should ordinarily be placed back in the post she occupied before going on leave.
If that position has ceased to exist for genuine and demonstrable organisational reasons, the employer must provide another role that is as close as reasonably possible to the original one in terms of pay, grade, status, responsibilities, managerial authority and opportunities for career progression.
What the case is about
The ruling came on a petition filed by Chartered Accountant Rakhi Bisht, who claimed that her professional position was adversely affected after she informed her employer about her pregnancy and subsequently returned from maternity leave.
Bisht had about 14 years of professional experience when she joined the organisation in 2022 as Manager, Accounting, drawing a monthly salary of Rs 2.60 lakh, according to an ANI report.
As per her case, she informed the management about her pregnancy in May 2023 and was later moved to another team. She went on maternity leave in December 2023 and returned to work in July 2024.
After resuming duty, she was informed that her previous position was no longer available and was instead placed in the Treasury Department. Bisht alleged that the new assignment was substantially inferior to the managerial accounting responsibilities she had earlier handled. She also claimed that she was given no reporting staff and was kept out of managerial meetings.
What the company said
The employer denied Bisht's allegations, saying there had been no change in her designation, level, salary or seniority.
It maintained that, following an organisational restructuring, she was given investment accounting and currency revaluation responsibilities while continuing at the same managerial level.
Creche availability
The issue of the creche facility at the workplace was also considered by the High Court.
Bisht had approached the employer about the availability of a creche in September 2024. She was initially told that no such facility was available at that time. The employer subsequently took the position that a creche did exist, but was not functional on the days relevant to her request.
The High Court held that merely having a creche facility is not enough if it cannot actually be used when an employee requires it. A facility that is non-functional at the relevant time does not meet the statutory requirement under Section 11-A of the Maternity Benefit Act.
Why Delhi High Court ruled in favour of the woman
The Court said an employer cannot comply with the law on paper by retaining a woman's salary and designation while taking away meaningful responsibilities, decision-making authority or future career opportunities. Doing so, it observed, would effectively permit the employer to accomplish indirectly something that cannot be done directly under the law.
The High Court also clarified the scope of Section 12(1) of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961. The provision bars an employer from changing the conditions of a woman's service to her disadvantage during the period of her statutorily protected absence. According to the Court, this protection is not limited to cases where employment itself is terminated.
The phrase "conditions of service", it said, encompasses the substantive elements of a person's employment. This includes the nature and substance of the duties assigned, grade and functional position, reporting structure, supervisory responsibilities, as well as the employee's consideration for appraisal and promotion.
"Retention of the same designation and remuneration is, therefore, necessary but not by itself sufficient" where other aspects of employment are changed to the employee's detriment, the Court held.
Such an interpretation would turn Section 12 into little more than a formality and undermine the purpose of maternity legislation, the Court said. The legislation is intended to safeguard the dignity of motherhood, economic security and a woman's professional standing.
The Court found inconsistencies in the employer's own pleadings and communications. It noted that the employer had said Bisht's earlier position had been assigned to another employee who was promoted while she was away on maternity leave. An internal communication placed before the Court also referred to assigning activities to Bisht merely to "keep her engaged" after her return.
The Court ordered respondent no. 2 to pay Bisht compensation of Rs 10 lakh, besides Rs 1.5 lakh towards costs. While determining the compensation, it took into account her professional standing as a Chartered Accountant, her approximately 14 years of experience and her monthly salary of Rs 2.6 lakh. The compensation, the Court noted, was roughly equal to four months' salary.
The compensation and costs have to be paid within eight weeks. If the payment is not made within that period, the amount will attract interest at 9% per annum from the date of the judgment until it is realised.
The Court therefore held that, as a general rule, a woman returning from maternity leave is entitled to be restored to the position she held before her leave.
If that position has genuinely become unavailable because of demonstrable organisational reasons, the employer must offer an alternative that is substantially equivalent. The comparison cannot be limited to salary alone and must also take into account grade, status, role, responsibilities, managerial authority and prospects for career advancement.
The employer is also required to explain to the woman, before she returns to work, why her previous position is no longer available. It must also spell out the details of the role being offered in its place, including the grade, remuneration, reporting structure and duties attached to it.
If the employee raises an objection to the proposed arrangement, the employer has to consider it and convey its decision in writing, along with reasons for that decision.
The Court also made it clear that a woman can herself request changes to her duties, working hours, workplace, work pattern or even seek an alternative role after returning from maternity leave.
However, such a request cannot subsequently be treated as her acceptance of reduced service conditions or as a waiver of the statutory protection available to her. Nor can the arrangement be held against her when her appraisal, increment or promotion is considered.
The employer had challenged the maintainability of the petition under Article 226, arguing that the matter arose from a private employment relationship and concerned contractual conditions of service.
The High Court did not accept this contention. It held that Bisht was not asking the Court to enforce a contractual provision, but was seeking protection available to her under Section 12 of the Maternity Benefit Act.
The Court also referred to Section 27 of the Act, which gives its provisions an overriding effect over any inconsistent terms contained in an employment contract. On that basis, it held that an employer cannot avoid a statutory obligation simply because it is a private entity.
The High Court further turned down the argument that Bisht had an alternative statutory remedy. It said the case raised questions involving fundamental rights and constitutional issues relating to equality, dignity and maternity protection. The Court also noted that the relevant rules and schemes under the Code on Social Security, 2020 had not yet been framed.
The High Court also issued broader directions concerning maternity safeguards that could affect private employers. It directed the Union of India to use its powers under Sections 149, 150 and 154 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 to frame rules or schemes, or issue directions, aimed at ensuring effective implementation of maternity protections.
The proposed framework is to address several areas, including workplace accommodation related to pregnancy, protection of an employee's role and status after maternity leave, lactation support, disclosure and functioning of creche facilities, timelines for dealing with maternity-related grievances, safeguards against retaliation and the designation of authorities empowered to receive and decide complaints, including requests for urgent interim protection. The exercise is to be completed within six months from the date of the judgment.
The framework contemplated by the Court would also require pregnancy-related accommodation requests to be assessed in writing. It would provide safeguards against compelling an employee to take leave or accept an inferior position, require reasoned written decisions where an employee's role or reporting structure is affected, and protect employees from retaliation.
In its concluding observations, the Court said the constitutional protections under Articles 14, 15, 21 and 42, read together with maternity legislation, mean that pregnancy and motherhood cannot be allowed to result in professional disadvantage.
The petition filed by Bisht was accordingly disposed of with the declarations, compensation and directions set out above.

briefs.headline: Rise of ‘digital hawala’ aiding money laundering, terror financing, global watchdog says
briefs.deck: FATF report identifies the fusion of virtual assets with the traditional 'hawala' system as a significant development; it says that nearly 70% of surveyed jurisdictions have reported the integration of new technologies into such networks
briefs.bodyText:
A centuries-old underground banking system is now transforming into a tech-enabled network, with virtual assets adding new layers to “digital hawala”. The shift is being exploited for purposes ranging from routine money laundering to, in some cases, financing terrorist organisations, the latest Financial Action Task Force (FATF) report said.
The global money laundering and terror financing watchdog’s report, titled “Investigating Professional Money Laundering, Underground Banking, and the Use of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers”, identifies the fusion of virtual assets with the traditional “hawala” system as one of the most significant developments. According to the report, nearly 70% of surveyed jurisdictions have reported the integration of new technologies into such networks.
Six forms of ‘digital hawala’
The study has flagged six forms of “digital hawala” — a term covering a spectrum of technologies that facilitate the coordination, execution, settlement, or concealment of transactions.
One configuration involves digital coordination but traditional settlement, with operators using encrypted messaging applications, shared ledgers and online platforms to communicate instructions, recruit clients and couriers, and maintain records. The second is a “digital customer interface”, such as mobile wallets or fintech apps, although settlement between operators happens via cash or trade in both cases.
The next is virtual asset-based settlement, where stablecoins are used to settle balances directly. In the “integration with formal digital infrastructure” configuration, funds are moved via payment service providers, fintech platforms, and virtual International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs).
The fifth is artificial intelligence-based tools for automated transaction structuring, dynamic mule-account routing, and high-speed fiat-to-cryptocurrency conversion. The last one involves “hawala” apps, which may be bundled digital ecosystems combining messaging, cloud storage, social media, Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), lending apps, and even gaming platforms.
The FATF found that these configurations make transactions faster, more opaque and more complex, while expanding the network’s reach and resilience. The report said that digitisation is acting as a catalyst for traditional settlement mechanisms rather than replacing them, with cash remaining critical at the collection and exit points.
Turkiye case study
It cited a case study of Turkiye’s discovery of a “digital hawala” network financing the terror group, the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL). In 2023, raids on a self-described ISIL “administrative officer” led to the seizure of about $57,250 in cash, followed by a further $5,54,000, along with “hawala” notebooks and digital transfer receipts. A jeweller and two mobile phone shops operated as fronts, and the transfers were disguised as charity donations.
Turkiye also reported the use of VASPs, Over-The-Counter brokers, and mule accounts, with jewellers and precious-metals dealers serving as cover. The FATF survey analysis found that such hybrid methods were progressively replacing or complementing cash/trade-based settlements in West Asia.
The shift to digital tools has made it harder for law enforcement agencies and financial intelligence units (FIUs) to trace networks through interpersonal links due to the use of access-controlled platforms by perpetrators, the report said. In response, the FATF has recommended greater use of technology in investigations, noting that Indonesia’s FIU uses blockchain analytics to trace virtual-asset flows where unlicensed transfer services intersect with crypto assets.
The FATF found that strong anti-money laundering/counter-terrorist financing enforcement and bank “de-risking” (severing financial transactions with high-risk jurisdictions) were themselves pushing genuine users and even licensed money service businesses into the informal channels often used by criminals. Therefore, it cautioned against overly punitive enforcement.
Observing that most jurisdictions did not have reliable data on the scale of underground banking, the report has flagged inconsistent use of terminology, such as “hawala”, as an impediment to cross-jurisdiction cooperation. It recommended disrupting entire laundering chains rather than individual transactions. Underground banking systems should be given a clear legal status, either integrated into licensed financial services or explicitly criminalised, it said.
The report states that nearly 90% of surveyed jurisdictions reported “hawala” networks operating within their territory, and over 80% now named them as a principal channel for professional money laundering. Over 60% rated such networks as a heightened risk in national assessments.
Quoting an example, it said the Netherlands’ Operation Klaver exposed a single underground banking operation that processed about €500 million in criminal proceeds over eight months, using couriers, counting warehouses, coded ledgers and international brokers.
Professionalisation is reshaping the networks into hierarchical and business-like structures run through formal management practices and digitised record-keeping. Lawyers, accountants, auditors, notaries and real-estate agents are increasingly being roped in, as per the report.
